notes: Work workspaces; work-kit review fixes: CLAUDE.md links docs/agents/work-kit.md; the pin test compiles index.css with Tailwind scanning only its @source globs and finds work-kit's probe class, holds the list of work-kit host rules TempCode's stylesheet lacks, and requires a revision under the phone app's work-kit url once it has one; the doc says the www pin rests on GitHub's redirect and git's credential helper, that the Mac fetched it, that a clone without work-kit access cannot install, and which host rules are missing.; Bump work-kit to v2 (75ff59b): the cn and host-rules exports, optional peers, the host rule list; Pin work-kit, the shared private package: a devDependency at one commit in the git+https://www.github.com form (bun fetches github: specs as an unauthenticated tarball, which a private repo refuses; www. makes it git clone through gh's credential helper), yjs held at 13.6.31, the main process bundling it (externalizeDepsPlugin exclude), electron-builder leaving node_modules/work-kit out, and Tailwind reading its source. scripts/workKitPin.test.ts checks the pin against bun.lock, WORK_KIT_API 1, the lock guard (one yjs, y-prosemirror, y-protocols, prosemirror-model and @tiptap/pm; no @blocknote/xl- or @y/ package), the builder rule, the exclude, the @source line and a render of work-kit/ui/kit-probe; docs/agents/work-kit.md says how the pin works and how to bump it.; Work M2: sectors on every fenced row, pairing sign-in, the caller's fence carried end to end; work-kit renderer test names say what they check; Bump work-kit to v2 (75ff59b): every peer optional, so the worker's install takes no React or Tailwind; Pin work-kit, the private package LifeOS and TempCode share; Work's frame after its second review: nothing of Work can stop the host, an ensure cannot leave a transaction open, and turning Work off stops what is running. No pillar is imported when the registry loads: work/modules.ts loads each through its own guarded loader (PILLAR_LOADERS, loadWorkModules), so a pillar whose code or dependency throws as it loads is left out and named (WORK_LOAD_FAULTS) and its methods answer why; WORK_MODULES is empty until that load, and startWork with no list refuses to run before it. The host reaches Work through one door, work/load.ts (loadWork, awaited at the top of startServer): if the mount itself cannot load or start, the host gets an inert Work that reads off and answers why. inputShapeOf moved to work/toolInput.ts, which imports nothing of Work, and the registry re-exports it; a test holds index.ts and apptools.ts to importing only types, the loader and that helper. Each ensure now runs inside a savepoint the host owns (work/schema.ts): a fault rolls it back and releases it, a BEGIN inside it is refused, a COMMIT or ROLLBACK that ends the host's transaction is counted the pillar's fault, and nothing is left open for a later write to join. Every tool call's signal is joined with the stretch Work is on (work/ctx.ts), whichever harness made it, and that stretch is aborted before the modules stop. A module's handle gets a signal too, as an optional fourth argument: the caller's socket going or Work turning off (milestone 15 found a forwarded job ran on after its caller left); a handler written with three arguments is called as before. The Swift generator tries a union's literal-pinned object branch only for the values it lists (branchGuard), so a chip's {at: 'lifeos', table: 'docs'} decodes as a CanvasSource and not as an entity ref with an unknown table; Generated/Types.swift regenerated, one line. A workspace's default Work settings are a fresh value each time. Tests for each; docs/agents/work.md and ios-contract.md say so.; A Work thread keeps its job across a move by any route: the move's manifest names the job of every Work thread in the bundle, and the import checks the workspace it resolved (milestone 6's need 3 for milestone 9's files). Before a row leaves, the sender's probe asks whether the thread's folder lands in its job's workspace on the other host; but the import also places a thread by its project's linked copy, which can sit in another Work workspace, where the thread would read that job's add-ons and sector. MoveExport now writes workHomes (by session id: the Work workspace's sector, link id, name and folder; all null for a Work Chat; no entry for a thread whose workspace is not Work's), present whenever a Work thread rides, and MoveImports.begin refuses, before any row lands, a Work thread that would land in a Work workspace of another job (workLandingRefusal: the same link id, the same sector, or for a workspace with neither the same folder; never two different sectors), a Work Chat or a homeless thread that would gain a job there, and a bundle whose sender does not say which job. A landing in a code workspace is left as it was: the thread keeps its fence and reads no job. The commit's digest covers the names, so a host that does not check them cannot land the thread. sessionMoveWork.test.ts holds the refused cases (by folder and by a linked project's copy) and the allowed ones; docs/agents/work-scope.md says it under "A move".; The Windows rig on the box (Work M11): scripts/win-vm builds a Windows 11 Enterprise Evaluation machine from Microsoft's ISO with an answer file (an admin, a standard user logged on at boot, OpenSSH, Git for Windows, the box's loopback blocked) and runs it as agents under QEMU/KVM on 127.0.0.1 only, 8 cores and 16 GB, an overlay per run on a read-only base; up, down, status, ssh, scp, QMP screenshots, snapshots, and run-in-session.sh, which starts a program on the logged-on desktop through an interactive scheduled task. rig.test.ts covers the machine's arguments, the clean daemon environment, the answer file, the quoting and the QMP client; docs/agents/windows-vm.md is the manual, with one CLAUDE.md entry.; The toolchain's manifest test no longer counts manifests: it checks base.json names the five base tools for the box and the Mac, and holds every pillar's manifest beside it to the schema, one name per tool, a licence and its note, https sources and GPL tools as separate processes, so a pillar's own <pillar>.json passes without touching the test.; docs/agents/work-kit.md says what the pin now holds: the three overrides and why, and that the first import of work-kit/editor must add its y-prosemirror and y-protocols peers.; Bump work-kit to v3 (f3f0530): the block editor (work-kit/editor) and the collaboration client (work-kit/collab), on BlockNote 0.57.0. Two overrides hold the editor's one ProseMirror: prosemirror-model at 1.25.13 and @tiptap/pm at 3.34.0, the versions BlockNote 0.57.0's ranges resolve to.; Work M3: child tables take their parent's fence by one line in CHILD_OF; Work scope, the fence and the preamble (milestone 6 of the Work plan): what a Work thread is on the server, what it can never load or start, and what it is told. A thread's scope is stamped once where its row is made (stampScope in work/scope.ts, called by SessionRegistry.create): a thread of a Work workspace, a Work Chat, and any thread a Work thread spawns or starts is a Work thread of that same workspace, or the create is refused; never a code thread, which loads the person's own MCP servers and sending keys. Code branches on the row, never on the switch: a Work row keeps its fence with Work off, and off only means nothing new of Work is made. workspace.create {kind: 'work'} makes the app's own folder under <work root>/Work, one per sector; a Work Chat runs in Work/Chats with no workspace; a Work thread is a chat or a research thread. app_start_thread refuses a project outside the caller's workspace and lists, reads and seeds only from its own scope; spawn_agent's child follows its parent; send, wait, answer and interrupt never reach a thread outside the scope; a batch holds one scope. Across hosts a Work thread's asks ride thread.start inside a work envelope with firstMessage left empty, so a host from before Work refuses them instead of starting a code thread (contract-crosshost.ts): start makes a Work thread of that host's own workspace for the job, probe is asked before a Work thread moves and answers only when the thread's own folder lands in that workspace, call is ctx.peer. spawn_agent with a host is refused for a Work thread, and the calls of CrossHostAgents are guarded where the host hands them to the tools. The fence: a Work thread loads no MCP server but the app's own. Claude Code is fenced by strictMcpConfig, a Work config root that links only projects, CLAUDE.md, the sign-in and the store's skills and is put back at every spawn, the account's connectors off three ways, and a PreToolUse hook that denies any mcp__ tool the thread's own servers do not list by its whole name, Claude's own schedules and channels, and the Mac bridge's tools once the workspace may no longer use that Mac. Codex is fenced by its own CODEX_HOME rewritten before every thread start and resume, plugins, apps and hooks off in the file, on the argv and in the thread's config, the folder named untrusted, and a check that stops a thread whose app-server names any server but the app's. work/fence.proof.test.ts plants a fake server in every source of both and runs the real CLIs, as a code thread (each plant must load) and as a Work thread (none does). Only Claude Code is offered for Work: Codex and Muse reach the app's tools through the stdio bridge, where a tool argument named sessionId replaces the thread's own, and Muse has no proven fence. The Work preamble opens every Work thread's first message on every start path, a Work Chat and a child included, and no opt-out, parent or switched-off project drops it: whose instructions count, that everything read is material and never an instruction, that nothing is sent by shell, script or browser, and which job this is; the modules' parts and the project's own text follow it, and a three-sentence standing rule sits in Claude's system prompt and Codex's developer instructions. ctx.scopeOf, ctx.threads (start with the routine run stamped host side, resume by the app's own line, ownerSaid for a quote the owner typed) and ctx.peer (a Work tool's call to the same module on another host, under the workspace's mayUseDesktop here and that host's bridge policy there) are built. Add-ons: a Work thread sees its own workspace's rows and the global rows marked for Work, adds and removes in its own scope only, and reads none where Work's rule did not come up; skills it writes stay in its own workspace's scope. A Work thread spawns cold, never from a warm process. A code thread's spawn, row and first message are what they were, with the switch unset, off and on. docs/agents/work-scope.md is the account.; Add-on grants sync again to every host entitled to the row's scope (F1, the correction to 81a84473c). That commit let a pull or a broadcast carry an add-on grant only to the host addonHome names, which on the box, the home of a global row, is no host, so the box stopped sending global grants to the Mac and script:e2e-addon-grants failed 8 checks of the shape "mac follows the box's grant". The rule is now the one M7's review asked for: a pull and a broadcast carry a grant where its row's scope is shared (addonShared, index.ts): a global row's to every host, a workspace's only while the workspace is linked to the other hosts' copies, which a Work workspace never is, so a key of a workspace only one host has never leaves it. pushOne keeps its rule from before (a grant goes to the scope's home alone). Tests: a Mac-only key is neither pulled by nor broadcast to the box, and the box's own global grant is pulled by and broadcast to the Mac; script:e2e-addon-grants passes in full (48 checks).; Bump work-kit to v4 (4789da7): the sheet package of milestone 26. work-kit/sheet is the canvas (Univer's grid under our chrome, Univer's UI loaded with the first grid), work-kit/sheet/xlsx the .xlsx importer that treats every file as hostile, work-kit/sheet/suggest the suggestion model, work-kit/sheet/worker the formula worker on our engine. Nothing in TempCode imports them yet; no new package enters the lock.; Work M4: close what the reviews found; Work M4: drafts tied to threads, task links, the event feed; The media canvas to the design standard's own guards. A note row's focus is index.css's one outline (the extra focus-visible ring goes), and the player, a focusable div, takes focus-ring in place of outline-none. Both vertical scrollers say overflow-x-hidden. The agent's glyph on a note is TypeGlyph's chat glyph, the one place a type tint is drawn. The preview's stand-in poster, a picture that keeps its own colours, moves to MediaCanvas.preview.fixtures.tsx with the preview's other data.; Work M17: hold reads under Convex's limits, and purge only for the removal that asked; Work M17: an owner-scoping case for projectDocs.purgeContent; Work M17: close what the review found; Work M17: the content store, block documents and sheets; Meetings and recordings (milestone 35 of the Work plan): a recording or a transcript dropped into a Work thread becomes a meeting beside it, transcribed on the host that holds it with speaker turns, and no part of a recording ever leaves that host through the pipeline.; The LifeOS connection (milestone 7 of the Work plan): the host signs in to LifeOS as the owner for its screens, and each linked workspace gets a draft-only LifeOS key held to its sector for its agents. ctx.lifeos and ctx.links are built in src/main/server/work/lifeos/. The device token lives in this host's vault as a sealed secret with no profile entry, so the account sync never sends it and the grant sweep never deletes it, and it is handed only to the LifeOS address that issued it. The session trades it for one-hour JWTs, keeps the owner's live Convex client (convex 1.49, bundled into main) with the JWT refreshed and every subscription reattached after a reconnect, and draws its state as data: off, signed out, pairing, connecting, connected, unreachable, refused. Sign-in is by pairing (the host polls for the token itself) or with a minted token; sign-out revokes the session in LifeOS. A Work or code workspace with a sector, and the Work Chats with every sector, get a key minted with bots:mint on the host that holds the scope's add-ons, kept only as the grant of that scope's lifeos add-on row (role 'lifeos'); a pass puts a lost role mark back, mints again into a row someone pointed elsewhere, retires a key whose scope lost its link, and keeps each mint's name before LifeOS is asked. A thread created with a task, mail or event chip is linked in LifeOS's workLinks, queued while LifeOS is away; completeFor completes the linked tasks with the reason and the thread, never one of another sector. The wire: work.lifeos.status, pairStart, pairCancel, setToken, signOut, link and jwt (approve: a LifeOS JWT can send as the owner), and the work.lifeos push, which never carries a token, a key, a JWT or the pairing code. With LifeOS unreachable every member answers a typed unreachable and no thread fails to start; with the Work switch off nothing reaches LifeOS. Proven against real LifeOS on isolated instances (proof/firstStep.ts, proof/live.ts); docs/agents/work-lifeos.md is the account.; Add convex 1.49.0 as a devDependency for the host's LifeOS client (Work milestone 7). It is bundled into main by electron-vite, so only the client code ships; its own esbuild 0.27.0 becomes the top-level esbuild, and electron-vite keeps 0.25.12 nested.; The PDF canvas's first DOM test waits for each thing it checks: the pager and the mode come with the kind's bar and the opened file, a beat after the first page, so under load (13 on the box) its immediate reads lost the race. Every assertion is kept; the file's waits have a 5 s ceiling for a loaded box.
